result.text:
I built a LinkedIn scraper this afternoon that finds our next 1,000 waitlist signups. Total cost: about $5/month.

Here's the playbook we're running at @GoodEnoughAi.

When Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash yesterday, the entire comment section under the launch posts was engineers talking about one thing: better AND cheaper. Those people are our exact customers. We sell managed open-source models at 70-90% less than frontier pricing. Someone reacting to a "cheaper model" post is raising their hand in public.

So instead of buying lead lists, we scrape the hands.

The stack:
→ Apify no-cookie actors scrape reactions + comments off any LinkedIn post ($2 per 1,000 people, zero account risk, no burner logins)
→ Apollo enriches each profile URL into title, company, headcount
→ A scoring pass filters for our ICP: US builders, heads of AI, data eng leads, agencies
→ Top matches get a human look, the rest flow into outreach
→ Everything lands in our Notion, nothing sends without approval

Built the whole thing with Claude Code in one session. First run pulled 217 people off a single post. Today's batch is 7 posts (the Gemini 3.7 launch wave plus open-model releases) for about 1,000 prospects, at a cost of roughly $2.

One rule we learned the hard way: only scrape posts under a month old. We pulled a 2024 post first and got 200 people whose "intent" was two years stale: fresh engagement or nothing.

Distribution isn't about reach; it's about finding the people already telling the market they want what you sell.

DM "scrape" and i'll shoot over the entire strategy.
